As a 340B Covered Entity, Shawnee uses savings generated through participation in the 340B Drug Pricing Program to support and strengthen our mission of providing comprehensive healthcare and supportive services to underserved and vulnerable populations.  The program enable us to stretch scarce federal resources, allowing us to expand access to care, improve patient outcomes, and maintain critical services that would otherwise be financially challenging to sustain.  Our 340B savings are reinvested directly into the operations and infrastructure necessary to serve our patient population.  These expenditures support both healthcare delivery and the social determinants of health that significantly inpact patient well-being.  A portion of our 340B funds is used to support essential operational expenses and facility improvements that ensure a safe, reliable, and efficient environment for patient care.  These investments include major capital projects such as the replacement and maintenance of HVAC systems, which help maintain proper environmental conditions for patient services, staff operations, and medication storage and the staff that support these functions.  This fiscal year alone, we have had to repair a large parking lot, install three HVAC systems, and fix a roof on our largest clinic.  We also utilize 340B funds for vehicle purchases and maintenance necessary to support transportation services, home visits, medication delivery, and other community-based programs.                                                                    Pharmacy Operations:  340B program savings help offset pharmacy expenses that are not fully covered by Medicaid or other reimbursement sources.  This includes pharmacy staff salaries and fringe benefits for pharmacists, pharmacy technicians, and support personnel who are essential to medication management, patient counseling, prescription processing, and compliance activities.  Byu funding these positions, we are able to maintain pharmacy services that improve medication access, adherence, and overall patient outcomes.  Additionally, 340B funds support pharmacy courier services that facilitate medication delivery to patients who may face transportation barriers, mobility limitations, or geographic challenges.  These services help ensure timely access to medications and reduce interruptions in treatment.  Transportation Services:  Transportation is a significant barrier to healthcare access for many of our patients.  To address this need, we use 340B savings to support transportation drivers and transportation-related services that enable patgients to attend medical appointments, obtain medications, and access other necessary healthcare and community services.  These programs help reduce missed appointments, improve continuity of care, and support better health outcomes.  We have purchased four vehicles that are used to enhance access.  Recognizing that stable housing is a critical component of health, we invest 340B resources in housing support services.  Housing aides assist patients with housing-related needs, helping them maintain stable living environments and access supportive resources.  These services are particularly important for individuals facing economic hardship, chronic illness, behavioral health challenges, or other complex needs that can affect their ability to achieve and maintain optimal health outcomes.
